findings: ID, title, 2026-10-26 v1 date, sections I-VIII, sole Table I, Figure 1 caption, two formulae and 31 references match the frozen extracted paper.
The notes cover the full available paper rather than only the abstract; no appendix is present in this frozen available body.
Reading coverage and character counts are text-reading evidence only, not provider token usage or image/PDF inspection.

Correctly separates structural/historical/experiential memory and the proposed SQLite graph, embedding/HNSW retrieval, content-hash watcher, weighted semantic controller, pinned nodes and explicit page-safe envelope.
The scoring weights, semantic eviction advantage and 15% context threshold are described as design/research hypotheses rather than tuned or proven policy.
Correctly distinguishes E4 vector/graph substrate from E5 lexical SQLite prototype with four of nine tools; E5 does not implement the whole proposed controller.
Text portability does not establish embedding/ranking portability or actual serving-prefix cache hits; notes explicitly preserve both qualifications.

E1: six repositories, 17.6M cl100k_base tokens/70MB, 4.17 bytes per token; 4GB text/8GB indexed text and 119/298/469TB fp16 GQA KV estimates are represented as storage extrapolations, not runtime/cost measurements.

E2: 752 selected Python fixes, up to 300 per repo, non-merge and at most 20 Python files, median two edited files; one-hop closure medians 32 files/114532 tokens/2.7% Django, 24/4.6% scikit-learn, 2/9.9% Flask are accurate and explicitly only a proxy.

E3: 852 commits and 3695 co-edited file pairs; 23.5% direct, 52.0% transitive, 52.7% with naming links, 47.3% disconnected; random 0.9% direct and 16.3% transitive are accurate. Co-change is not equated with causal dependence or necessary reading.

E4: synthetic million-node/440M-token/five-million-edge/384-dimensional workload, 3.7GB, build under four minutes, CPU laptop, 200 retrievals, median 1.70ms/p99 2.76ms and two-hop median 0.95ms are accurate. This is substrate feasibility without retrieval quality, controller overhead or freshness maintenance cost.
E5: eight bugs, Sonnet writer then context-reset Haiku reader, same symptoms and pre-fix trees; file-level root-cause identification is distinguished from correct patches and test passing.
Table I is transcribed accurately: A 6/24,18 calls,6.5 reads,196.6K input; B 21/24,9,5,43.3K; P 8/8,8,4.5,41.7K; C 14/16 and164.4K per call. A/B have three trials per task, P one and C two.

4.5x lower B reader input and 3.8x C/B input are scoped to the reported medians and different tool conditions. Writer median83K tokens across eight successful investigations is separately disclosed; all-role amortized/output/cache/monetary costs remain unmeasured.

Single-sided Fisher p=1.3e-5 is correctly attributed to authors; repeated trials on eight tasks create clustering/pairing concerns. Equal observed B/C87.5% is not equivalence or non-inferiority evidence; pooled8/8 does not prove long-run accumulation safety.
The notes correctly treat A/B as a limited inherited-note contrast and P as a tiny pooled-memory probe, not isolated evidence for every designed component.

No independent component ablations establish page envelope, failure versus rca content, co-change edges, semantic scores, eviction or HNSW quality. Plain session-summary carryover is missing, lexical baseline and note-quality confounding remain.

RQ1-RQ5 are future plans, including multi-session SWE-bench success, useful-edge retrieval, semantic eviction versus LRU, negative knowledge removal and cross-model/framework generalization. These are not reported results.
Notes preserve Python-only scope, current graph versus older commits, keyword-selection bias, closure proxy, synthetic E4 and small two-repository same-task E5 rediagnosis.
No exact model version/configuration or confidence claim is invented beyond the paper. All-success writer selection/quality and absence of plain-summary baseline constrain generalization.
Wrong-note contamination, web write-back injection, summary faithfulness and team sharing remain open. Raw author package and reference claims were not independently verified.
The memo proposes evaluation questions for existing MemoryLedger failure/correction records, directed handoffs and explicit pagination instead of asserting an implementation benefit.
Reuse of the existing ledger, unique TASK/navigation and retained corrections/disagreements is compatible with the checked SYSTEM-99 boundaries; no new writable parallel task chain is proposed.
HNSW/MCP/controller/agent_doc migration are deferred pending real repository quality and full-cost evidence. Dependency freshness hashes are not equated with automatic correction propagation.

The paper cannot close actual host loading, all-input usage, final task quality, full fees, concurrency/recovery or the ongoing SYSTEM-99 batch; no repository token or latency gain is inferred. This is an assessment of the note scope, not a source-code audit.
Review completed before the original deadline on first reserved attempt; no retry, refund, old gate reset or second attempt was used.

Only local static text/hash reads and this review JSON write were performed. No network, experiment, model invocation, package installation, paper code or repository code execution occurred. Python standard-library hashing/serialization is review bookkeeping, not a paper experiment.
No source, guide, TASK, frozen producer evidence or historical gate was modified. Output ownership is restricted to .agent-runs/stratum-review-1116/review.json.
This manual independent review is not a trusted-runtime review receipt, empirical-result validation, publication authorization or automatic reading-credit assignment.

acceptance_scope: The frozen reading.md/source.json accurately and critically summarize the full available frozen Stratum v1 body, including E1-E5 denominators, costs, missing ablations and repository adoption limits. Accepted solely as a manual static independent reading-note review.

optional_comments.comment: A useful optional detail for a later edit is that the paper says A typically exhausted a 16-round tool budget; table median18 calls counts calls rather than rounds. The present note makes no mistaken equality and needs no correction.
